skill.name: system-environment-setup
skill.description: Configure development and production environments for consistent and reproducible setups. Use when setting up new projects, Docker environments, or development tooling. Handles Docker Compose, .env configuration, dev containers, and infrastructure as code.
skill.summary: Generate Docker Compose, environment, dev container, Makefile, and Terraform templates for reproducible project setup.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown or sample-code false positives, including code fences, localhost URLs, relative links, private CIDRs, and normal process.env access. I confirmed credential-handling risks where the skill shows copy-paste database URLs with weak passwords and secret-like provider keys in environment templates. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious command execution.

remediation.suggestion: Replace postgres:password and POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password with generated placeholder syntax and require unique local passwords.
Use neutral placeholders and document secret managers or cloud identity roles for AWS, Stripe, SMTP, and token secrets.

remediation.issue: Terraform state can retain sensitive values
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for encrypted remote state, restricted state access, and secret references for database passwords.

Users may copy these values into real projects instead of generating unique secrets.

content.value_statement: Project environments drift when services, secrets, and tooling are configured by hand. This skill provides setup templates for Docker Compose, .env files, dev containers, Makefiles, and Terraform.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Docker Compose services for Node.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Nginx.
Creates .env.example structures and Node.js environment loading patterns.
Defines VS Code dev container settings for a Docker Compose workspace.
Adds Makefile targets for install, development, testing, migration, and cleanup.
Provides AWS Terraform examples for VPC, RDS, ECS, and load balancing.
limitations: Provides templates and guidance; it does not provision infrastructure by itself.
Requires review before use with production secrets, ports, or cloud accounts.
Examples are Node.js and AWS oriented, so other stacks need adaptation.
Generated commands can change local files, containers, and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Start a New Service
use_cases.description: Create local service scaffolding with Docker Compose, environment variables, and repeatable commands.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Onboarding
use_cases.description: Give new contributors a consistent dev container, setup guide, and common project commands.

use_cases.title: Prepare Infrastructure Templates
use_cases.description: Draft Terraform and configuration files before a platform engineer hardens them for deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Create Local Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Docker Compose based local setup for my Node.js app. Include PostgreSQL, Redis, and a safe .env.example.

prompt_templates.title: Add Dev Container
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a VS Code dev container for this repository. Use the existing Docker Compose services and list required extensions.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Environment Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my environment setup. Replace weak defaults, separate development values from production values, and explain required secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Full Stack Environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible environment for a multi-service app. Include Docker Compose, Makefile targets, Terraform structure, and production hardening notes.

Makefile commands for common development tasks.

output_examples.input: A team lead wants faster onboarding for new contributors.
output: A dev container plan connected to project services.
A project structure checklist for setup files.
A short runbook for install, start, test, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer wants a first Terraform draft for AWS.
output: A Terraform outline for networking, database, and compute resources.
A list of values that must come from secure secret storage.
Warnings about state encryption and access controls.

best_practices: Generate unique local secrets before starting services, even for development.
Keep .env files out of version control and commit only sanitized examples.
Review Terraform state storage, access controls, and encryption before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse example passwords or token secrets in shared environments.
Do not expose database, Redis, or SMTP ports beyond the network that needs them.
Do not run cleanup or volume removal commands without checking project scope.

faq.question: Does this skill run Docker or Terraform automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and commands that a user or agent must review before running.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Only after replacing defaults, locking down networks, and moving secrets to approved storage.

faq.question: Which stacks does it fit best?
faq.answer: It fits Node.js services with Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, Redis, dev containers, and AWS Terraform.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets securely?
faq.answer: It identifies where secrets belong, but teams must provide their own secret manager and access rules.

faq.question: Can Codex or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that edit project files.

faq.question: What should I review first?
faq.answer: Review credentials, exposed ports, destructive Makefile targets, and Terraform state settings.
